transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Um, well, what finally made me make an appointment and ask for help is that I just keep forgetting little things I normally handle without an issue. Like returning phone calls, or turning in a registration form... which reminds me, the last form I had to fill out was for this community center thing, and they changed their whole online system last month. It is just a complete nightmare to navigate now. My sister tried to sign up for a ceramics class on there and it double-charged her credit card, so she had to spend like two hours on the phone with her bank just to get it sorted out. She makes really nice bowls, though. But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah, just forgetting stuff like that, or I'll tell myself to stop for an errand on the way home from work and then completely blank on it until I'm already pulling into my driveway.
Did you experience similar problems with attention or forgetfulness when you were a child?

Yeah, actually. Even back in elementary school, I was always that kid. You know, the one who constantly forgot permission slips or somehow lost my homework somewhere in the black hole of my backpack. I remember I had this one Lisa Frank backpack, the one with the neon dolphins? I loved that thing so much. My mom bought it for me at this little stationery store that used to be downtown, but they closed years ago to build a frozen yogurt place. Which is a shame, because their fro-yo isn't even that good, it always tastes kind of icy, you know? Anyway, um... oh, right, school. Yeah, I always needed my mom or my teachers to remind me step by step just to finish my projects. Otherwise, I'd just get completely off track.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still for long periods?

Um, I guess a little? Like, if I have to sit through one of those longer classes—I take some evening professional development ones for my job—I definitely notice myself clicking my pen a lot. Or I'll be bouncing my foot and just constantly shifting around in my chair, even when I'm really trying hard to just sit still and pay attention. 

Speaking of pens, actually, I just ordered this new brand of gel pens for the office. I'm an admin assistant, so I do all the supply ordering, and these new ones are just amazing. They write so smoothly, not like those cheap ballpoint ones that always leave little ink globs on the side of your hand. My boss is left-handed, so he absolutely hates the ones that smear everywhere. He's been in a really weird mood lately anyway because his daughter is moving out to Oregon, which is a huge change for them, but... wait, sorry. Did I answer your question? I just know I bounce my foot and fidget with my pen when I'm stuck in a chair for too long.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or cutting in while they are speaking?

Um, no, I don't really think I do that. If anything, I'm usually the one getting interrupted. Like my coworker, Brenda. She is constantly talking over me in the office, especially lately because we're trying to figure out the catering for the office holiday party. We ordered from this local Italian place last year, and they completely forgot the garlic knots. Which is crazy, right? Who forgets the bread? They gave us a discount code for next time, but honestly, I don't even know if we'll use it because their marinara sauce was way too sweet anyway. I prefer a more savory sauce, you know, with a lot of fresh basil. My grandmother used to grow huge pots of basil on her back porch, and it always smelled so good in the summer... wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, interrupting. Right. No, I usually just wait my turn to talk.
Do you often feel restless on the inside, like you're constantly 'on the go' or driven by a motor?

Um, no, not really. I don't feel like I'm driven by a motor or anything. I actually get pretty tired by the end of the day, honestly. Especially after sitting at my desk for eight hours. My chair at work is just terrible for my back. I keep meaning to ask HR for one of those ergonomic ones, the ones with the mesh backs? My friend Sarah has one at her job, and she swears by it. She works at this marketing firm downtown, and they have all these crazy perks, like a ping pong table in the breakroom and free snacks. They even have cold brew on tap, which sounds amazing, but I'd probably drink way too much of it and never sleep. I already have a hard time sleeping sometimes because my neighbor's dog barks at literally everything that walks by. It's a little terrier mix, I think. Super cute, but just so loud. But um... yeah, no, I don't really feel restless on the inside like that. Just regular tired, I guess.
